previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, and a history of recent Klebsiella UTI was admitted for body twitching lasting 24 hours. She reported a prior similar episode with gabapentin and had recently been restarted on it for neuropathy. Labs showed elevated glucose but no uremia or infection signs. Gabapentin was discontinued, and she underwent scheduled hemodialysis, after which symptoms resolved. Asymptomatic bacteriuria was noted but not treated due to recent antibiotic completion and lack of symptoms. She was discharged home with instructions to avoid gabapentin and follow up with her primary care provider.

Please call the access clinic at ___ if you have fevers

Please also monitor for incisional redness, drainage or 
bleeding, arm swelling or increased pain at the access site or 
any other concerning symptoms.

You should check the left arm access daily for a thrill (buzzing 
sensation) and if this is not present, you should call the 
access clinic right away and not wait until your dialysis 
session.

may be left open to air. The arm may be gently washed but do not 
submerge or soak the arm. If there is a small amount of drainage

help the swelling decease.
